terra.problem: Eliphaz being one of Job’s three friends is a fact from Job 2:11, outside this passage, and needs a reference.
Eliphaz being one of Job’s three friends is a fact from Job 2:11, outside this passage, and needs a reference.
Saying Job lifted people up instead of lecturing them adds a contrast the text does not make.
Eliphaz being one of Job’s three friends is a fact from Job 2:11, outside this passage, and needs a reference.
The text says Job’s words steadied people who stumbled, not that they held people together.
Saying crowns and thrones were not on Eliphaz’s mind claims to know what he was thinking.
The last two sentences repeat that Eliphaz said it without adding an explanation or Papa Dorin’s personality.
Calling it the voice’s question to Job suggests the voice addressed Job. Eliphaz reports what he heard, but the passage does not identify the voice’s audience.
The voice says people dwell in houses of clay, not that people are called houses of clay.
Taking the harvest even from the thorns does not establish that nothing is left or that it is all gone.
Nobody leaving a crumb adds that the entire harvest is taken, which the text does not say.
Eliphaz goes on to say man is born to trouble, not where he thinks trouble comes from.
After the quote, the explanation merely repeats that it is Eliphaz’s advice and adds a generic exclusion of elders.
The explanation restates the verse and then says it is all in one verse, without adding a meaningful explanation or Papa Dorin’s voice.
Job having lost so much is a fact from outside this passage and needs a reference, such as Job 1:13–19.
Full vigor and many descendants do not establish that Job will not be alone or forgotten, so the answer is not necessarily the opposite of Eliphaz’s picture.
